The archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive. hatchzip.dev | Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a desktop app and a command line tool. It extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, for when there is not enough disk space to extract an archive next to itself, such as a large game download on a nearly full disk. Download it from hatchzip.dev. A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. title: Snapintosh/Snapintosh
body:
EL2 hypervisor and toolchain that boots macOS on the ASUS A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite), with an Adreno Metal/IOGPU stack

README 節錄：# Snapintosh Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor (hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple devices the kernel looks for. Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack written for this project: - **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in. - **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the internal panel. - **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno. There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path. The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID), native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage controller. Snapintosh is used together with q1n1, a UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2 after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which drives Snapintosh from there. ## Status This is experimental software, written for one laptop model. |

body:

README 節錄：# gdirect 中文 · Changelog gdirect browses, downloads, uploads and mounts your Google Drive from the terminal. It finds Google IPs that are reachable from your network and sends Drive traffic straight to them, with multi-connection, resumable downloads. ## How it works | Traffic | Route | | --- | --- | | Drive API, downloads, uploads and their token refresh (`browse`, `ls`, `download`, `upload`) | A scanned Google IP. The hostname and certificate check stay the same.
